edition.witness_note: Lake 1912 Loeb copy-text; Lightfoot/Funk middle recension not yet locked as second witness

source_text: [1] Περὶ δὲ τοῦ συνδούλου μου Βούρρου, τοῦ κατὰ θεὸν διακόνου ὑμῶν ἐν πᾶσιν εὐλογημένου, εὔχομαι παραμεῖναι αὐτὸν εἰς τιμὴν ὑμῶν καὶ τοῦ ἐπισκόπου: καὶ Κρόκος δέ, ὁ θεοῦ ἄξιος καὶ ὑμῶν, ὅν ἐξεμπλάριον τῆς ἀφ̓ ὑμῶν ἀγάπης ἀπέλαβον, κατὰ πάντα με ἀνέπαυσεν, ὡς καὶ αὐτὸν ὁ πατὴρ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ ἀναψύξαι, ἅμα Ὀνησίμῳ καὶ Βούρρῳ καὶ Εὔπλῳ καὶ Φρόντωνι, δἰ ὦν πάντας ὑμᾶς κατὰ ἀγάπην εἶδον. [2] ὀναίμην ὑμῶν διὰ παντός, ἐάνπερ ἄξιος ὦ. πρέπον οὗν ἐστὶν κατὰ πάντα τρόπον δοξάζειν Ἰησοῦν Χριστὸν τὸν δοξάσαντα ὑμᾶς, ἵνα ἐν μιᾷ ὑποταγῇ κατηρτισμένοι, ὑποτασσόμενοι τῷ ἐπισκόπῳ καὶ τῷ πρεσβυτερίῳ, κατὰ πάντα ἦτε ἡγιασμένοι.
pass_a_gloss: As for my fellow servant Burrus, your godly deacon, blessed in all things, I pray that he may remain for your honor and the bishop's. And Crocus too, worthy of God and of you, whom I received as a sample of your love, has refreshed me in every way; so may the Father of Jesus Christ refresh him as well, together with Onesimus and Burrus and Euplus and Fronto, through whom I saw all of you in love. May I always have joy of you, if indeed I am worthy. So it is fitting in every way to glorify Jesus Christ, who glorified you, so that, made complete in one submission, being subject to the bishop and the presbytery, you may be made holy in every respect.
pass_b_english: About Burrus, my fellow servant and your godly deacon, blessed in everything: I pray he may stay on, to your honor and your bishop's. Crocus, too, worthy of God and of you, whom I welcomed as a sample of your love, has refreshed me in every way. May the Father of Jesus Christ refresh him in turn, along with Onesimus, Burrus, Euplus, and Fronto. Through them I have seen all of you, in love.

May I always have joy of you, if I am worthy. It is right, then, to give glory in every way to Jesus Christ, who has given glory to you, so that, knit together in a single obedience and subject to the bishop and the presbytery, you may be holy through and through.

choices.term: ὡς καὶ αὐτὸν ὁ πατὴρ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ ἀναψύξαι
choices.english: May the Father of Jesus Christ refresh him in turn
choices.why: ἀναψύξαι is an aorist optative: a prayer, not a prediction.
rejected: as the Father ... shall also refresh him (ANF; future)

choices.why: Latin loanword for a copy or sample; Crocus is a living specimen of the church's love.

choices.english: knit together in a single obedience
choices.why: καταρτίζω is to mend or fit together; one submission joins them.

anf_compare.notes: ANF inserts a full quotation of 1 Corinthians 1:10 ('in the same mind, and in the same judgment ... the same thing') that Lake's text does not print; ANF followed witnesses with that expansion. ANF also makes ἀναψύξαι a future ('shall refresh'), where the Greek is a wish.

variants: Lake prints no 1 Corinthians 1:10 expansion after κατηρτισμένοι; ANF's English reflects a fuller reading. Second witness not yet locked.
notes: Whole chapter 2 (sections 1-2) matches the ANF span, except the quotation ANF adds.
κατηρτισμένοι may echo 1 Corinthians 1:10 (ἦτε δὲ κατηρτισμένοι); kept as possible, not inline. ANF's 1 Corinthians 16:18 for 'refreshed' is also only a possible echo.

review.notes: Checked paragraph [1] (sections [1]–[2]) against Pass A and Pass B. Greek «Περὶ δὲ τοῦ συνδούλου μου Βούρρου, τοῦ κατὰ θεὸν διακόνου ὑμῶν ἐν πᾶσιν εὐλογημένου, εὔχομαι παραμεῖναι αὐτὸν εἰς τιμὴν ὑμῶν καὶ τοῦ ἐπισκόπου» matches A «As for my fellow servant Burrus, your godly deacon, blessed in all things, I pray that he may remain for your honor and the bishop's» and B «About Burrus, my fellow servant and your godly deacon, blessed in everything: I pray he may stay on, to your honor and your bishop's». «ὅν ἐξεμπλάριον τῆς ἀφ̓ ὑμῶν ἀγάπης ἀπέλαβον, κατὰ πάντα με ἀνέπαυσεν, ὡς καὶ αὐτὸν ὁ πατὴρ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ ἀναψύξαι, ἅμα Ὀνησίμῳ καὶ Βούρρῳ καὶ Εὔπλῳ καὶ Φρόντωνι, δἰ ὦν πάντας ὑμᾶς κατὰ ἀγάπην εἶδον» matches A «whom I received as a sample of your love, has refreshed me in every way; so may the Father of Jesus Christ refresh him as well, together with Onesimus and Burrus and Euplus and Fronto, through whom I saw all of you in love» and B «whom I welcomed as a sample of your love, has refreshed me in every way. May the Father of Jesus Christ refresh him in turn, along with Onesimus, Burrus, Euplus, and Fronto. Through them I have seen all of you, in love». Optative prayer and condition hold: «ὀναίμην ὑμῶν διὰ παντός, ἐάνπερ ἄξιος ὦ» / A «May I always have joy of you, if indeed I am worthy» / B «May I always have joy of you, if I am worthy». Purpose clause holds: «ἵνα ἐν μιᾷ ὑποταγῇ κατηρτισμένοι, ὑποτασσόμενοι τῷ ἐπισκόπῳ καὶ τῷ πρεσβυτερίῳ, κατὰ πάντα ἦτε ἡγιασμένοι» / A «made complete in one submission, being subject to the bishop and the presbytery, you may be made holy in every respect» / B «knit together in a single obedience and subject to the bishop and the presbytery, you may be holy through and through». No negation reversed; Father remains agent of ἀναψύξαι; no inline citation is present to mismatch; title names the submission thought, not a bare locus. «your bishop's» and dropped «indeed» are stylistic, not sense reversals.

Source identity: Paragraph [1] is Ignatius Ephesians 2, matching the named edition and locus. Completeness: All clauses from the Locked Greek are rendered in Pass A and B, including the prayer for Burrus, the description of Crocus, the list of refreshers, the joy conditional, the glorification of Christ, the submission to bishop and presbytery, and the sanctification. Negation: No negation present; preserved by absence. Agency: Clear agency in 'I pray', 'he has refreshed me', 'may the Father refresh', 'you may be made holy'. Modality: Optative εὔχομαι, ἀναψύξαι, ὀναίμην, ἐάνπερ preserved as prayers and conditionals in Pass A/B. Doctrine: Christ's glorification of believers, ecclesiastical order (bishop/presbytery), and sanctification are accurately conveyed. Scripture: No inline scripture citations in the Locked Greek; lemma note on κατηρτισμένοι echoing 1 Cor 1:10 is appropriately treated as a possible echo, not an added citation, per rules. Title: 'Knit together in one obedience' captures the thought of κατηρτισμένοι ἐν μιᾷ ὑποταγῇ, not merely a locus. Pass A fidelity: Every clause's sense is preserved. Pass B adds neither nor contradicts A or Greek. Covered source paragraphs: [1]. No uncertainties or reasons for fail.
